text:
alyssa: Heads-up — eu-west dedicated-silo-17 (rack n0-n3) is hitting socket starvation on n0. 99th% decode latency spiking to ~1.2s, and a noticeable fraction of requests are spilling back to shared-pool. Connection queue length reported >256 on inference-proxy. Anyone digging? :eyes:
jamal: On it. Which exact nodes and do we have recent proxy/haproxy logs or netstat output?
alyssa: Affected tenant: retail-recs on reserved slice rs-17. Model: open-llama-13b-q8_0. Not every node — seems limited to nodes with high ephemeral connection churn after last deploys (rolled yesterday).
infra-bot: ALERT: eu-west-n0-inference-03 high SYN_RECV / listen backlog drops (sysctl somaxconn=128). Incident id INC-3423.
sophia: Pasting quick netstat/ss snippets: ```tcp        0      256 0.0.0.0:443            0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      1234/haproxy``` and `ss -s` shows backlog drops: `TCP: inuse 120 orphan 0 tw 300 alloc 380 mem 14` — plus haproxy stats show accept queue fullness spikes.
jamal: That aligns with accept() returning EAGAIN in the proxy logs. Also seeing `accept() failed: Too many open files` around the same timeframe. Looks like listen backlog + file limits + accept hot-loop causing starvation.
kevin: Cost note: when dedicated slices spill to shared-pool the per-token cost goes up and P99s degrade for both dedicated customers and shared users. We saw a 2x share spike in the last hour. Avoid large restarts that force retries into shared.
sophia: Quick mitigations I propose: bump `net.core.somaxconn=1024` and `net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048` on the hot nodes, increase haproxy listener backlog and tune `--maxconn`. Also enable SO_REUSEPORT on proxy listeners to distribute accept load across workers. Will canary to two nodes first. :wrench:
ops-bot: Runbook queued: apply-sysctl-canary -> targets: rs-17-n0-01, rs-17-n0-02 -> expected rollback window 10m -> notifier: #eng-infra
jamal: Executing canary now. Commands: `kubectl exec -n infra infractl -- sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024` and `kubectl exec -n infra infractl -- sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048`. Also `systemctl kill -s HUP haproxy` after updating haproxy.cfg to bump backlog/reuseport.
alyssa: After canary, monitor: proxy conn_queue, haproxy `show stat`, and the model tail latency metric. If stable for 15m, roll incrementally to remaining n0 nodes in rs-17.
sophia: Longer-term: autoscaler logic should smooth reconnect storms when tenants redeploy to avoid synchronized SYN bursts. Also consider a lightweight connection warm pool per tenant to keep steady connections (reduces churn).
kevin: Also create a billing impact ticket to capture cost delta from spillback. If we do a global knob change, evaluate cost/benefit vs per-slice tuning.
alyssa: I'll open an incident doc and a runbook entry. Assigning to @jamal and @sophia; tagging @sre-oncall for awareness. :spiral_notepad:
jamal: Canary completed on rs-17-n0-01/02 — P99 latency returned to baseline, backlog drops stopped, and no spillback to shared observed. Beginning staged roll to remaining n0 nodes at 17:14 UTC.
sophia: Adding a probing metric: `tcp_listen_drop_count` (custom exporter) and a new alert when backlog drops > 5/min per node. Also adding a dashboard panel for accept queue length and haproxy accept EAGAIN counts.
alyssa: Nice work. Follow-ups: validate haproxy config for SO_REUSEPORT and open fd limits (`ulimit -n`), add a scale test for simultaneous tenant redeploys to catch this in CI, and schedule a short postmortem after the incident doc is filled. :thumbsup:
